samples.question: The picture shows six columns standing on one long black baseline. Each column is a vertical stack of grey squares of the same size, resting on the baseline, and the stacks differ only in how many squares they hold; every stack holds between one and six squares. Directly below the baseline, under each column, sits one round coloured disk, its TAG. The six tags are red, orange, green, blue, purple and brown, one of each, and which tag sits under which column changes from picture to picture. A single black triangle above the row points down at exactly one column: that is the POINTED column, the one whose centre the triangle is nearest to. Read the picture in two steps. First count the grey squares in the pointed column and call that number K. Second, ignore the pointed column and count columns from the LEFT edge of the picture, so that the leftmost column is number 1 and the rightmost is number 6, and go to column number K. The answer is the colour of the tag under that K-th column. K is a position, never a colour and never a height: the pointed column's own tag, the tallest stack, the shortest stack, the leftmost and the rightmost columns are each the answer only as often as chance allows, and the triangle marks where to start reading rather than what to report. The pointed column is sometimes itself the K-th column and usually is not. Which tag colour does this pick out? Answer red, orange, green, blue, purple or brown.
